question: What is the primary public health goal of contact tracing during an infectious disease outbreak?

options.A: To enforce legal penalties on individuals who fail to report symptoms
options.B: To conduct mass vaccination campaigns across urban populations
options.C: To replace hospital-based care with community-managed isolation
options.D: To break transmission chains by locating and managing exposed individuals

explanation: Contact tracing focuses on finding people exposed to an infected person so they can be monitored and managed before spreading the disease further. [learn more](GST114_U2_T18#GST114_U2_T18_h1)

question: Why does contact tracing represent a shift from passive to active healthcare management?

options.A: It brings health workers into the community to find cases rather than waiting for sick people to arrive at hospitals
options.B: It eliminates the need for laboratory diagnostic confirmation during outbreaks
options.C: It transfers clinical decision-making authority entirely from doctors to community leaders
options.D: It relies on automated digital tracking systems instead of human interaction

explanation: Active surveillance involves health personnel proactively seeking out potential cases in the community instead of waiting passively for patients to present at clinics. [learn more](GST114_U2_T18#GST114_U2_T18_h1)

question: Which link in the chain of infection is directly targeted and interrupted by contact tracing?
explanation: By identifying and separating exposed individuals before they become infectious, contact tracing stops the pathogen from transmitting to a new host. [learn more](GST114_U2_T18#GST114_U2_T18_h2)

question: What role does the incubation period play in planning a contact tracing protocol?

options.A: It calculates the total number of hospital beds needed during a surge
options.B: It determines the duration for which identified contacts must be monitored or quarantined
options.C: It establishes the geographical boundaries of the affected community
options.D: It identifies the exact laboratory test required to confirm the pathogen

explanation: The incubation period dictates the maximum time window a person might develop symptoms, which defines how long they need active monitoring. [learn more](GST114_U2_T18#GST114_U2_T18_h2)

question: Which criterion typically defines a high-risk or close contact during an outbreak investigation?

options.A: Face-to-face interaction within one meter for more than 15 minutes
options.B: Residing in the same municipal local government area as the case
options.C: Passing by the infected person briefly in an open outdoor corridor
options.D: Working in the same large multi-story commercial building

explanation: Close contact definitions generally rely on physical proximity and duration of exposure, which substantially raise the likelihood of pathogen transmission. [learn more](GST114_U2_T18#GST114_U2_T18_h3)

question: Why is it clinically necessary to categorize contacts into high-risk and low-risk tiers?

options.A: To assign legal liability for the initial transmission event within the community
options.B: To determine whether the index case requires surgical or medical intervention
options.C: To simplify the statistical data entry required for national health bulletins
options.D: To optimize the allocation of limited public health resources toward individuals most likely to develop disease

explanation: Categorization allows health teams to focus intensive monitoring, testing, and quarantine enforcement where the risk of secondary transmission is highest. [learn more](GST114_U2_T18#GST114_U2_T18_h3)

question: What is the most effective approach when interviewing an index case about their daily movements?

options.A: Demanding a written log before beginning any verbal conversation
options.B: Involving local law enforcement officers to compel truthful answers
options.C: Employing a strict interrogative tone to ensure the patient does not lie
options.D: Using a supportive tone with open-ended questions to encourage open recall

explanation: A supportive, non-judgmental approach builds trust and helps patients remember details they might otherwise hide out of fear or stigma. [learn more](GST114_U2_T18#GST114_U2_T18_h4)

question: A patient appears defensive and expresses fear that their employer will find out about their diagnosis. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Reassure the patient regarding strict confidentiality protocols and privacy protections
options.B: Explain that the employer must be notified immediately by law to protect coworkers
options.C: Threaten mandatory institutional quarantine if they refuse to cooperate
options.D: Postpone the interview indefinitely until the patient calms down on their own

explanation: Addressing fears of stigma and reassuring patients about confidentiality is essential to secure their cooperation during contact tracing interviews. [learn more](GST114_U2_T18#GST114_U2_T18_h4)

question: What is the primary operational difference between quarantine and isolation?

options.A: Quarantine is voluntary, whereas isolation requires a court order in every instance
options.B: Quarantine applies only to bacterial infections, while isolation applies only to viral pathogens
options.C: Quarantine restricts exposed individuals who are not yet sick, while isolation separates sick individuals who are infectious
options.D: Quarantine is managed in a hospital setting, while isolation is managed exclusively at home

explanation: Quarantine is for healthy people who had exposure, while isolation is for those who have confirmed or suspected active illness. [learn more](GST114_U2_T18#GST114_U2_T18_h5)

question: Why is providing logistical support such as food and communication credit essential for successful home quarantine?

options.A: It removes the necessity for individuals to leave their homes for basic supplies, ensuring compliance
options.B: It guarantees that the patient will recover from the illness without requiring medication
options.C: It replaces the need for daily temperature checks and symptom reporting
options.D: It fulfills legal requirements mandated by international trade organizations

explanation: People cannot successfully stay home if they lack food or water; supporting their basic needs makes adherence to quarantine feasible. [learn more](GST114_U2_T18#GST114_U2_T18_h5)

question: What is the primary ethical risk of breaching a patient's confidentiality during contact tracing?

options.A: It automatically invalidates all laboratory test results in the affected region
options.B: It destroys community trust, causing people to hide symptoms and avoid public health workers
options.C: It increases the biological mutation rate of the infectious pathogen
options.D: It prevents health workers from accessing essential medical supplies from the government

explanation: When confidentiality is broken, fear of stigma causes individuals to conceal illnesses, which undermines entire disease control efforts. [learn more](GST114_U2_T18#GST114_U2_T18_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT an acceptable ethical practice for nurses engaged in contact tracing?

options.A: Explaining the rationale for quarantine clearly before enforcing restrictions
options.B: Disclosing the name of the index case to contacts to convince them of the exposure risk
options.C: Balancing community safety needs with respect for individual autonomy
options.D: Protecting patient health records from unauthorized viewing by coworkers or neighbors

explanation: Nurses must never reveal the identity of the index case; contacts can be warned of exposure without knowing who infected them. [learn more](GST114_U2_T18#GST114_U2_T18_h6)

question: What is a primary logistical challenge to contact tracing in many urban Nigerian settings?

options.A: Excessive availability of private vehicle transport for all residents
options.B: Imprecise residential addresses and high population mobility
options.C: A complete absence of mobile telecommunication networks
options.D: Mandatory international travel restrictions between states

explanation: In many dense areas, lack of formal street naming and frequent movement make physically locating contacts difficult. [learn more](GST114_U2_T18#GST114_U2_T18_h7)

question: Why is collaborating with local leaders and traditional rulers essential for successful outbreak control in Nigeria?

options.A: They hold community trust and help reduce suspicion and resistance against health workers
options.B: They are legally mandated to replace government nurses during a crisis
options.C: They manage the financial budget for international health organizations
options.D: They possess formal medical degrees required to diagnose infectious diseases

explanation: Involving respected community figures bridges the gap between public health teams and local residents, securing cooperation and dispelling rumors. [learn more](GST114_U2_T18#GST114_U2_T18_h7)
